X.finding: Model APPROVE triggers payment with no adjuster or amount check
X.why: TriageService.java:66-67 calls payments.pay with the model's amountClaimed/currency when autoApprove, and application.yml:9 sets auto-approve: true; the report names both locations and the unchecked, unbounded amount.
Raised inside finding 1: TriageResult.java:4 amountClaimed is double and PaymentService.java:16/20 Payment/pay use double.

X.finding: Re-posting the same claim pays it twice (no idempotency)
X.why: ClaimsController.java:27-31 re-runs triage on every POST and TriageService.java:66-67 pays again with no check for an existing payment, so PaymentService.instructions gets duplicates; it only arises on the K2 auto-pay path.

X.finding: Claim email concatenated into the system prompt
X.why: TriageService.java:36-41 appends email to the prompt and :51 passes it as .system(prompt); the report gives the injected-APPROVE payload and that, with K2, an attacker pays themselves.
application.yml:7 holds api-key: claims-prod-9f2c4e1a7b3d8e60, read via @Value at TriageService.java:27. The quoted commit hash can't be checked here (no git history in the folder).

X.finding: Model summary and claimId pasted into HTML (XSS)
X.why: ClaimsController.java:35 produces text/html and :39/:41 concatenate claimId and r.summary() unescaped; the report says model output from a public email can carry a script.

X.finding: temperature(0.0) gets a 400 on Haiku 5.5, so every call fails
X.why: TriageService.java:50 sets temperature(0.0) with model claude-haiku-5-5 (application.yml:6); the report says the model answers a non-default temperature with a 400 and all 5 attempts fail (hedged 'if so', but the 400 for this model is stated).

X.finding: Content read before checking stopReason (refusal / 512-token cut-off)
X.why: TriageService.java:55 reads content().get(0).text().get() with no stopReason() check and :49 caps maxTokens at 512; the report names both the refusal (NoSuchElementException) and the truncation cases.

X.finding: Prompt, answer and SDK error messages with personal data logged
X.why: TriageService.java:56 logs prompt (the whole email) and answer at INFO; :59 logs e.getMessage(). Both lines cited.

X.finding: Client built per attempt, no timeout, 5 retries over SDK retries
X.why: TriageService.java:46 builds a new AnthropicOkHttpClient per attempt with no timeout, inside the 5-attempt loop at :44 that wraps the SDK's own retries; both halves are named.

X.finding: catch (Exception) retries everything, drops the cause, ends as a 500
X.why: TriageService.java:58-59 catches every Exception and logs only getMessage(), and :63 throws IllegalStateException without the cause, which reaches the client as a generic 500 with no controller advice. The refusal-retry part overlaps K3.

X.finding: Input not bounded or validated, no rate limit
X.why: ClaimsController.java:18 ClaimRequest(String email) has no constraints and :28 has no @Valid; any size, or null, is sent to the model. It also notes the validation starter in pom.xml:19 is unused.
True that there is no src/test, but 'no tests' is on the answer key's Not defects list.

Y.finding: Claim email concatenated into the system prompt

Y.finding: Model output rendered as raw HTML (stored and reflected XSS)
Y.why: ClaimsController.java:35-41 serves text/html built by concatenating r.summary() and claimId (:39, :41) unescaped; the report says the model can be made to emit a script from the email.

Y.finding: Prompt, answer and SDK error text logged
Y.why: TriageService.java:56 logs the whole prompt (email) and answer; :59 logs e.getMessage().

Y.finding: Up to 15 calls per request, new client per attempt, no timeout
Y.why: TriageService.java:44 loop of 5 around the SDK's default 2 retries (5 x 3 = 15) and :46 builds a new client per attempt with no timeout; both halves named.

Y.finding: No stopReason check; refusal or max_tokens cut-off retried or Optional.get throws
Y.why: TriageService.java:55 reads content().get(0).text().get() without stopReason(); the report names the refusal and max_tokens cases.

Y.finding: catch (Exception) swallows everything; failures surface as a 500
Y.why: TriageService.java:58-59 catches all exceptions, including 4xx, and :63 throws IllegalStateException with no cause and no @ControllerAdvice, giving a generic 500 (stated across finding 6 and a should-fix note, recorded once).

TriageService.java:50 with claude-haiku-5-5 (application.yml:6); the report states the 400 on Haiku 5.5 and that every call then fails, though it hedges on whether 0.0 counts as non-default (it does: the default is 1.0).
TriageResult.java:4 and PaymentService.java:16 use double for the amount.

Y.finding: No input validation or bound, no rate limit
Y.why: ClaimsController.java:18/:28 has no @NotBlank/@Size/@Valid, so a null or 10 MB email goes to the model. The pom.xml:19 'validation starter unused' note restates this.
No src/test exists, but 'no tests' is on the answer key's Not defects list.

Y.finding: No authorization; anyone can overwrite any claim's result
Y.why: ClaimsController.java:27-35 has no auth and results.put at :30 is last-writer-wins, so anyone can replace the summary adjusters see; the pom has no security starter. Low for a demo module, and the payment harm is K2's.
ClaimsController.java:27-31 re-runs triage on every POST and TriageService.java:66-67 pays again with no check for an existing payment; it only arises on the K2 auto-pay path.

Y.finding: Prompt text has no version and no eval
Y.why: A process point about TriageService.java:36; the code alone can't show a defect.
TriageService.java:36-39 already offers REFER; telling the model to prefer it is a prompt-design preference.

Y.finding: Result store held in the controller
Y.why: ClaimsController.java:21 ConcurrentHashMap is demo storage (key's Not defects list); a layering preference.
True that PaymentService.java:25 has no caller in src/main, but that's a style opinion, not a defect.
